entityDescription:
Intellectual Property Institute Luxembourg (IPIL: www.ipil.lu) was established on August 1st 2014. IPIL is the official counterpart of Luxembourg’s IP Office. Its missions are to:
• coordinate the set-up of the public IP policy,
• develop and provide support services for enterprises, research actors, public institutions and other publics, 
• develop and provide training as well as promotion and awareness activities, 
• conduct projects and studies to provide advices to the authorities. 
IPIL is a spin-off company of the Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST: www.list.lu), that was based on former Henri Tudor Centre-CVT Department (created in 1994). It can count on a core, multicultural and multilingual experienced team of specialists (Luxembourgish, French, German, Spanish and Turkish) in their field of activity.
IPIL has developed IP-related services and activities that are provided to companies (with a special focus on start-ups, scale-ups and SMEs) as well as to Public Research Institutions and for patent and trademarks attorneys. These activities cover the whole range of IP matters, from industrial property to copyright and related rights and to soft IP. As the main actor in the country involved in IP awareness, training and services provision to economic actors and general public, it aims at developing IP and its exploitation including knowledge and technology transfer. 
IPIL develops its own and specific working tools, such as IP audit/diagnosis, IP information analysis methodologies, IP information searches methodologies, IP training scheme (e-learning and on-site) and develops related services that are proposed to companies.
Concerning those services to Luxembourg’s enterprises, IPIL is in charge of: 
• providing IP awareness raising activities and tools,
• providing IP support services, 
• organising IP training events,
• the national Patent Information Centre (Patlib network managed by the EPO).
Conscious of the importance of IP exploitation, IPIL is continuously investigating the state-of-the-art solutions developed and provided to companies, and is active in developing its own methodologies to help the national economy. 
Thanks to its proximity with the national IP authority and to proven years of experience within the framework of the EU-funded projects, IPIL has established sustainable and strong connections with the majority of the national and international IP offices (EUIPO, EPO, WIPO) in Europe, along with SME associations and business organisations.

EAT freedom GmbH & Co. KG is a German start-up specializing in healthy and gourmet full meals for adventurers who undertake long expeditions in extreme and highly stressful environments. For the development of its meals, the company constantly collaborates with groups of polar explorers, speleologists, high-altitude mountaineers, extreme sailors, and rowers to study and test the factors that influence food choices and habits during a mission. Examples are the organoleptic decay that occurs at altitude and the food fatigue that takes over as a stress factor after weeks of consuming a limited variety of dehydrated foods. Understanding the profound impact of food on a healthy and performing body and mind, EAT freedom uses premium quality ingredients for which it prefers low-temperatureprocessing, to preserve their full value, while offering a long shelf life. The start-up also focuses on the choice of whole grains, high-quality proteins, and healthy fats, makes limited use of salt and sugar, and ample use of herbs and spices to naturally enhance the flavour. In 2021-2022, the balanced recipes inspired by the Harvard Healthy Eating Plate found positive feedback in the collaboration with the European Space Agency for the supply of bonus food for the Minerva mission, during which the nutritional requirements set by the team of nutritionists and doctors supporting the mission were fully satisfied while meeting the astronaut's taste preferences.

The start-up was founded in 2021 by Dr. Sara Rocci Denis. Born and raised near Turin, she has always had a passion for exploration and mountaineering, which has led her to scale several peaks of 4,000m and beyond, her first at the age of 11. The idea of creating a line of gourmet meals that are quick to prepare and easy to transport, suitable for supporting high physical performance, was born in a tent in a high camp on Mount Cho Oyu, in Tibet, in 2011, where Rocci Denis, lacked the right nutrition to stay strong throughout the mission and to reach her adventure goal. In 2016, the meeting with Chef Stefano Polatomarked the formal beginning of the development of the prototype recipes. Chef Polato isa renowned food consultant who already developed bonus food for several astronauts prior to becoming Chef and Head of Food Development of EAT freedom project and developing with Dr. Rocci Denis the bonus food allowance for mission Minerva.

- Knowledge sharing space:- Apiary reports and notes

- Getting started boards for beekeeping novices
- Farmer and orchard grower partnerships

The features mentioned above provide a foundation to gaining complete insight into your apiary.
- They can help you save the time needed to perform your daily work - you no longer have to look inside every hive on a weekly basis
- Colony health reports and varroa detection will help you plan the necessary treatments and reduce the cost of loosing the bees

- Alerts and notifications will inform you if your immediate attention is needed
- Flowering phenology event notifications and flowering crop fields localisation near your apiary will help you locate the best spot to place your hives
- Beekeeping forums and boards are a great source of information if you are in a need of advice
- Farmer and orchard grover partnership program will help you get in touch with people in need of bee-aided pollination. Spirit AeroSystems is one of the world's largest manufacturers of aerostructures for commercial aircraft, defence platforms, and business/regional jets. Built on more than 100 years of aviation experience, Spirit is headquartered in Wichita, US, with ~14,800 employees globally. It has facilities in the US, UK (Belfast (Short Brother PLC) and Prestwick), France, Malaysia and Morocco.
With expertise in aluminum and advanced composite manufacturing solutions, Spirit’s core products include integrated wings and wing components, fuselages, pylons and engine nacelles. It also has a growing aftermarket and space business.
Spirit UK is one of the largest aerospace companies in the UK, with a total of ~ 3600 employees across its sites in Northern Ireland (c2,700) and Prestwick (c900). It is a major driver in the local economies where its sites are based. Spirit UK has over 700 approved UK suppliers, and is a key mentor in the aerospace industry’s SC21 supply chain development programme, working with suppliers to improve their competitiveness and win more high-value global work packages.
Spirit UK is a research-intensive company, and its two UK sites are centres of excellence for the design, manufacture and after-market support of complex aerostructures in metal and advanced composites, including wings, nacelles, fuselages and spoilers.
The principal activities of Spirit’s Belfast operations are the design, development, manufacture and assembly of major aircraft structural components (including wings, fuselages, engine nacelles and flight components) and provision of aftermarket component repair and overhaul, as well as other engineering services. Many of the programmes in which the company is involved has required significant R&D investment, including in the A220 advanced composite wing programme. At over �520m, this was the largest ever single inward investment in Northern Ireland, which will sustain over 1000 high-value jobs at peak production and many more in the UK supply chain.
Spirit Prestwick’s main activities are the design, development, manufacture and assembly of airframes, which consist principally of wing structure components. New product development includes design, development and materials research. Aerospace… is the technology driver for high-tech developments par excellence: smaller, lighter, more efficient and extremely energy efficient are not just keywords but the framework for each and every space project. entityDescription:
Planetum

Planetum is a brand of the contributory organization Observatory and Planetarium Prague, which includes two observatories (Stefanik observatory, Dablice observatory) and one planetarium in Stromovka.At observatories you can admire large telescopes. During the day you can look at the Sun using special telescopes, on clear nights you can observe the Moon, details of the planets, places where stars are born in the universe, or distant galaxies. In the planetarium, the universe is projected onto an artificial sky in the shape of a hemisphere. Both observatories and the planetarium have a rich selection of programs - from fairy tales for the little ones to documentaries on astrophysics and cosmology. You will also find unique interactive exhibits dedicated to the exploration of space and cosmonautics. You can sit in the cockpit of the space shuttle, explore the Apollo lunar lander and much more.
The planetarium is a time machine that can travel to the past and the future, a spaceship with which you can fly to the planets, among the stars or leave the Galaxy and look at our home from a distance of tens of billions of light years. All this thanks to modern digital technology that keeps moving forward. As early as 2023, the projection area will be transformed into a giant LED screen with an area of ​​867 square meters – the Prague Planetarium will have the first so-called LED-dome in Europe.
Planetum also became the first institution of its kind in the world to send its own satellite into orbit. The Planetum-1 satellite was launched on May 25, 2022, on a Falcon 9 rocket from Florida's Cape Canaveral. It is the first purely educational satellite in the world. In the foyer of the planetarium, you can take a look at its operations center.
